skills.name: Highest common factor
skills.description: The biggest number dividing both numbers.

skills.name: Lowest common multiple
skills.description: The smallest number both numbers divide into.

FM_GAVE_LCM.label: Gives the LCM when asked for the HCF
FM_GAVE_LCM.explanation: Mixes up 'highest common factor' and 'lowest common multiple'.

FM_HCF_IS_SMALLER.label: Thinks the HCF is always the smaller number
FM_HCF_IS_SMALLER.explanation: Says the HCF of 8 and 20 is 8, though 8 doesn't divide 20.

FM_LCM_IS_PRODUCT.label: Thinks the LCM is always the two numbers multiplied
FM_LCM_IS_PRODUCT.explanation: Says the LCM of 4 and 6 is 24 instead of 12.

FM_GAVE_HCF.label: Gives the HCF when asked for the LCM
FM_GAVE_HCF.explanation: Mixes up the two: answers 2 for the LCM of 4 and 6.

questions.prompt: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 12 and 18?
hints: A factor divides into a number exactly. List the factors of both numbers.
The HCF is the biggest number in both lists. It can't be bigger than the smaller number.
solution: The biggest number in both lists is 6.

questions.prompt: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
hints: List the multiples of each number: 4, 8, 12, … and 6, 12, 18, …
The LCM is the first number in both lists. It is often smaller than the two numbers multiplied.
solution: The first number in both lists is 12.

highest_common_factor.title: Highest common factor
highest_common_factor.big_idea: The HCF is the biggest number that divides into BOTH numbers exactly. It is never bigger than the smaller number, and it is only the smaller number if that number divides into the other.
steps: List all the factors of the first number.
List all the factors of the second number.
Circle the numbers in both lists.
The biggest circled number is the HCF.
highest_common_factor.sense_check: 8 doesn't divide into 12 exactly, so the HCF of 8 and 12 can't be 8. It's 4.

lowest_common_multiple.title: Lowest common multiple
lowest_common_multiple.big_idea: The LCM is the SMALLEST number that both numbers divide into. Multiplying the two numbers always gives a common multiple, but often not the lowest one.
steps: Write the first few multiples of each number.
Find the first number that appears in both lists.
Check: both numbers divide into it exactly.
lowest_common_multiple.sense_check: 4 × 6 = 24 is a common multiple, but 12 comes first in both lists.
